markdown_report:
The next step should test whether GRU4Rec’s apparent training separation depends on easy distractors. At 10% progress, a bounded candidate stress panel offers a practical extension of the existing temporal probe.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, all four categories pass the reported execution checks. This supports proceeding with behavioral diagnostics, although exported-predictor parity remains unmeasured. Second, Electronics has 14.49% sampled negative wins for low-frequency positives versus 2.86% for high-frequency positives. This motivates frequency-stratified investigation, without establishing a held-out deficit. Third, temporal-effect estimates are omitted. Their absence cannot justify adding recency mechanisms or treating temporal effects as zero.

**Insights from related work.** First, Krichene and Rendle show that sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons. Candidate construction therefore deserves explicit sensitivity analysis, while the pinned evaluator remains authoritative. Second, Prakash et al. report performance differences across item-frequency groups. Their results motivate stratification here, but do not establish the same mechanism in these datasets. Third, PURE distinguishes factual correctness from preference alignment. Title similarity can construct plausible distractors, but cannot label them irrelevant or reveal current intent.

These insights organize three directions: execution validity, candidate difficulty, and recurrent dependence. The framework separates what changes from what each measurement supports:

| Direction | Controlled change | Supported interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Existing temporal panel | History order; fixed candidates | Conditional order sensitivity |
| Proposed candidate panel | Distractors; fixed history and target | Conditional candidate sensitivity |
| Later recurrent probe | Intermediate hidden state | Local computational dependence |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality / future potential / code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency-matched candidate panel | 4 / 7 / 3 | Simple control; actionable frequency analysis | Established method; no direct ranking improvement |
| Title-similar distractor panel | 5 / 6 / 4 | Tests broad textual associations | Similarity is an imperfect relevance proxy |
| Hidden-state margin replay | 6 / 7 / 7 | Separates recurrence from scoring sensitivity | Requires architecture-specific instrumentation |

**Selected idea: frequency-matched candidate panel.** Reuse explicitly indexed training-prefix cases, freezing each history, target and checkpoint. Compare the existing uniform candidate set with 99 unique unseen negatives drawn uniformly from the target’s training-frequency band. Hold the trained model fixed; average repeated draws within users before category summaries. Report target-minus-maximum-negative margins, negative-win fractions and paired changes by target-frequency band. Report rank/HR only when the pinned ranking adapter is available.

Use local seed-42 generators and save candidate identities, exclusions and denominators. Insufficient pools remain unavailable. These are conditional training-prefix stress measurements, not official validation results, causal intent evidence or model improvements. Preserve one GRU4Rec checkpoint per category; select subsequent training changes only through unchanged host macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Extend the existing GRU4Rec diagnostic with a paired uniform-versus-frequency-matched candidate stress panel. Keep each training-prefix history, target, model checkpoint and scorer fixed, changing only the distribution used to draw 99 unique training-unseen distractors.
idea.motivation: Execution checks now pass, while the supplied temporal-effect values and official validation results remain absent. Electronics exhibits weaker sampled training separation for low-frequency positives, motivating a controlled test of candidate-distribution sensitivity before proposing architectural changes. This test does not assume that frequency matching makes candidates objectively harder or more relevant.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve existing probes and the separate twenty-user full-catalog recommendation workflow. Access the actual module through view.model and preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces. No unavailable metadata or review fields are needed.

Reuse the prespecified explicitly user-indexed training-prefix cases when available; otherwise construct them from public training histories using deterministic serialized-user ordering, final-training-interaction targets, the baseline truncation width and at least five retained prefix interactions. Never recover user identities from anonymous loader rows. Compute item interaction frequencies from the unchanged training split only, including all observed interactions. Define bands as 1–4, 5–19 and 20+, retaining these thresholds before inspecting results. These counts describe frequency, not exposure.

For each case, exclude the user's complete original training history, the target, padding and reserved IDs from negative eligibility. The matched pool additionally requires membership in the target's frequency band. Require at least 99 eligible items in both pools; do not broaden bands or sample with replacement to rescue a case. Report exclusions by category and target band. Compare both conditions on this same complete-case subset, and retain a separately labeled uniform summary for cases excluded from the comparison. If a frozen uniform set already exists, use it as uniform draw zero and generate four additional independent uniform sets. Generate five independent matched sets. Within each set, sample 99 unique items uniformly without replacement; overlap between sets and conditions is allowed. Keep the target first and save exact ordered candidate identities.

Use separate local SeedSequence namespaces incorporating seed 42, fixed category index, stable user index, condition and draw. Do not consume global training RNG streams. Score the history once and reuse its feature across candidate sets. Use the existing ModelView adapter; gather the maximum nonzero sequence position, never count minus one. Include all learned projections and biases through predict_score. Check finiteness and candidate-score shape. Preserve module training flags and global Python, NumPy, Torch and CUDA RNG states in finally, running inference under torch.inference_mode().

Primary statistics are target-minus-maximum-negative margin and the fraction of negatives scoring strictly above the target, with explicit denominators of 99. Define matched-minus-uniform negative-win fraction and uniform-minus-matched margin so positive changes indicate worse sampled separation under matched candidates. Include exact target tie counts. Rank and HR@10 require the pinned diagnostic ranking helper and documented tie convention; otherwise return null with a reason. Do not substitute a ranking convention. These diagnostic HR values are distinct from official host validation HR@10.

Average the five draws within each user and condition, compute paired user contrasts, and average users equally within each category. Report band counts, complete-case counts, category summaries and Monte Carlo standard errors for the independently sampled conditions. If uncertainty intervals are included, resample complete user records with all realized draws retained, using a separate seed-42 stream and 2,000 CPU bootstrap replicates; require at least 30 complete users. Label intervals selected-user reweighting intervals conditional on fitted checkpoints and realized candidates, excluding retraining uncertainty. Do not combine these intervals with Monte Carlo error as independent variance components. A four-category macro summary requires all four category outputs and gives categories equal weights; category-local macro fields remain null.

Update the interpreter to distinguish candidate sensitivity, sampled training fit and official validation performance. Unobserved negatives can be relevant, and frequency matching can make separation easier or harder. No title similarity, compatibility, mood, exposure or causal user-intent claims follow from this experiment.

This proposal changes diagnosis only and requires no retraining or predictor architecture change. Preserve exactly one independently trained GRU4Rec checkpoint per category, all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch and single-GPU execution. No independent scorer, fusion or checkpoint averaging is introduced. Record synchronized diagnostic runtime against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not read other trials, hidden test files or external datasets. No execution success or recommendation improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        saved = capture_module_modes_and_global_rng_states()
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            with inference_mode():
                existing = run_existing_family_specific_probes(train_loader)
                if not existing.required_execution_checks_pass:
                    return merge_unavailable_panel(existing, reason='execution checks failed')
                counts = count_interactions(self.view.user_train['History'])
                cases = reuse_or_build_prespecified_training_prefix_cases()
                records = []
                for case in cases:
                    uniform_pool = real_items_excluding_complete_training_history(case)
                    matched_pool = [i for i in uniform_pool
                                    if frequency_band(counts[i]) == frequency_band(counts[case.target])]
                    if min(len(uniform_pool), len(matched_pool)) < 99:
                        record_exclusion(case, pool_sizes=(len(uniform_pool), len(matched_pool)))
                        continue
                    features = compatible_log2feats(self.view, case.sequence)
                    final = gather_maximum_nonzero_position(features, case.sequence)
                    record = initialize_case_record(case)
                    for condition, pool in [('uniform', uniform_pool), ('matched', matched_pool)]:
                        for draw in range(5):
                            rng = local_rng(42, category_index, case.stable_index, condition, draw)
                            negatives = frozen_uniform_draw_zero_if_available_or_sample(
                                pool, n=99, replace=False, rng=rng,
                                condition=condition, draw=draw)
                            candidates = [case.target] + negatives
                            scores = self.view.predict_score(final, candidates)
                            require_finite_scores_and_expected_shape(scores)
                            record.save(candidates, scores,
                                margin=scores[0] - max(scores[1:]),
                                negative_win_fraction=mean(scores[1:] > scores[0]),
                                exact_target_ties=sum(scores[1:] == scores[0]),
                                rank_and_hr=pinned_rank_helper_or_null(scores, candidates))
                    records.append(record)
                save_trial_local_records_and_exclusion_counts(records)
                summary = average_draws_then_compute_paired_equal_user_summaries(records)
                summary.mcse = independent_candidate_stream_mcse(records)
                summary.intervals = conditional_paired_user_bootstrap_or_null(records, seed=42)
                summary.macro = None  # External aggregation requires all four categories.
                return merge_metrics_and_explicit_definitions(existing, summary)
        finally:
            restore_module_modes_and_global_rng_states(saved)

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return prompt_containing_measured_metrics_and_definitions(
        raw_diagnosis,
        limits=['conditional training-prefix candidate sensitivity',
                'frequency is not exposure',
                'unobserved candidates may be relevant',
                'missing measurements are not zero effects',
                'no causal intent or official validation improvement inference'])

originality.positive: Combines a fixed-history candidate intervention with explicit training-frequency matching and paired category analysis through the existing GRU4Rec interface.
originality.negative: Candidate stress tests and frequency stratification are established; the contribution is a focused diagnostic integration.

future_potential.positive: Can guide a subsequent single-model loss or sampling experiment by identifying where candidate-distribution sensitivity concentrates.
future_potential.negative: The panel does not directly improve recommendations, and training-prefix sensitivity may not predict official validation behavior.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses trained checkpoints, item scores and training histories without changing GRU internals or the exported predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable complete-case accounting, reproducible sampling, scorer compatibility and uncertainty reporting still require careful implementation.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can produce model comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog metrics.
Motivates documenting candidate construction and separating diagnostic sampling from the pinned selection benchmark.
limitations: Does not establish that frequency-matched negatives improve this GRU4Rec model.
Does not justify changing the host evaluator.

related_work.title: Prakash et al. (2024), sequential recommendation and item-frequency performance
contributions: The supplied search summary reports head, middle and tail performance differences concealed by aggregate results.
Motivates retaining target-frequency denominators and separate category summaries.
limitations: The supplied findings do not establish the same mechanism in the four Amazon datasets.
Training interaction frequency does not measure exposure or user preference.

related_work.title: PURE (2026)
contributions: The supplied search summary distinguishes factual correctness from personalized preference alignment.
Supports treating textual association and observed history as limited evidence rather than direct labels of current intent.
limitations: Does not validate frequency-matched candidate sampling.
Unavailable review-derived evidence cannot be imported into this task.
